job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

passage: Dear Diary, today in biology class, I learned that cells are the building blocks of life, but they are not all the same. My friend Rohan thought that an elephant must have giant cells compared to a mouse, but our teacher explained that organisms grow by increasing their number of cells, not by making individual cells larger. We also looked at onion peel cells under a microscope. I was surprised to see that even though plants need sunlight for photosynthesis, their root cells do not contain chloroplasts because they live underground. I used to think the nucleus was like a tiny brain that makes decisions, but the teacher clarified that it is actually a storage unit for genetic information, which acts as a blueprint for cell function. We also discussed bacteria, which are prokaryotic. Even though they lack a defined nucleus, they still possess DNA floating in their cytoplasm to carry out life processes. Finally, we learned that the cell membrane is not a solid, sealed wall; it is a selective, porous boundary that allows essential materials to move in and out. It is amazing how these tiny structures work together to keep us alive, whether we are a single-celled organism or a complex human being.

items.evidence: My friend Rohan thought that an elephant must have giant cells compared to a mouse, but our teacher explained that organisms grow by increasing their number of cells, not by making individual cells larger.
items.q: An elephant is far bigger than a mouse. What explains this difference?
options: It has many more cells than a mouse
It has much larger cells than a mouse
It has cells that never stop stretching
It has a bigger brain-like nucleus in each cell
items.explain: Organisms grow by increasing their number of cells, not by making each cell larger.

wrong.why: thinks bigger organisms have bigger cells
thinks growth means cells keep enlarging
thinks the nucleus is a brain that controls size

items.evidence: I was surprised to see that even though plants need sunlight for photosynthesis, their root cells do not contain chloroplasts because they live underground.
items.q: Meena looks at cells from a plant's root under a microscope. What will she find?
options: She will find no chloroplasts in them
She will find chloroplasts in every cell
She will find chloroplasts, since plants need sunlight
She will find chloroplasts only near the nucleus
items.explain: Root cells live underground, so they do not contain chloroplasts, even though plants photosynthesise.

wrong.why: thinks all plant cells have chloroplasts
guesses chloroplasts sit beside the nucleus

items.evidence: I used to think the nucleus was like a tiny brain that makes decisions, but the teacher clarified that it is actually a storage unit for genetic information, which acts as a blueprint for cell function.
items.q: Which comparison best describes the job of the nucleus?
options: A library holding the cell's instructions
A brain that decides what to do
A solid wall guarding the whole cell
An empty bubble that stores air
items.explain: The nucleus stores genetic information, a blueprint for the cell; it does not make decisions.

wrong.why: thinks the nucleus thinks like a brain
mixes the nucleus up with a sealed membrane
thinks cell parts are empty air bubbles

items.evidence: Even though they lack a defined nucleus, they still possess DNA floating in their cytoplasm to carry out life processes.
items.q: Sam says bacteria have no DNA because they lack a nucleus. Why is he wrong?
options: Their DNA lies loose in the cytoplasm
Their nucleus is just too tiny to see
Their DNA comes from the food they eat
Their DNA is stuck to the cell wall
items.explain: Bacteria have no defined nucleus, but their DNA floats freely in the cytoplasm.

wrong.why: thinks information can only be inside a nucleus
thinks bacteria cannot make their own DNA
mixes up the cell wall with where DNA is kept

items.evidence: Finally, we learned that the cell membrane is not a solid, sealed wall; it is a selective, porous boundary that allows essential materials to move in and out.
items.q: What would happen to a cell if its membrane let nothing pass through?
options: It would not get the materials it needs
It would be better protected and healthier
It would let the cell wall do that job
It would wait for the nucleus to decide
items.explain: The membrane is a porous boundary letting essential materials in and out; sealed, the cell gets nothing.

wrong.why: thinks a sealed skin is what a membrane should be
thinks the cell wall and membrane are the same
thinks the nucleus makes decisions for the cell
